description: The pie chart displays the domain distribution of the AttrEval-GenSearch test set, divided into twelve categories, each represented by a distinct colored slice with its percentage labeled externally via lines. The largest segment is 'AI/NLP Research' at 24.3%, shown in blue. Following it is 'Econ. & Fin.' at 18.4%, depicted in teal. 'History' and 'Game&Anime' are tied at 8.2%, shown in yellow and orange respectively. 'Daily Life' accounts for 7.1%, in light blue. 'Med & Health' and 'Science' each represent 6.7%, shown in green and light blue respectively. 'Business' is at 5.9%, in red. 'Pet & Animal' and 'Law' are close in size at 5.5% and 5.1%, shown in orange and pink respectively. 'Geography' and 'Math' are the smallest categories, at 2.7% and 1.2% respectively, shown in dark green and dark orange. The chart includes a legend-like labeling system with external lines pointing to each slice, and no slices are visually emphasized or exploded; the segments appear arranged in roughly descending order of size from the top right.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the domain distribution of the annotated AttrEval-GenSearch test set, encompassing twelve distinct categories. The largest category, 'AI/NLP Research,' accounts for approximately 24.3% of the dataset, followed by 'Econ. & Fin.' at 18.4%. 'History' and 'Game&Anime' are tied at 8.2%, while 'Daily Life' constitutes 7.1%. 'Med & Health' and 'Science' both represent 6.7%, with 'Business' slightly lower at 5.9%. 'Pet & Animal' and 'Law' are close in proportion, at 5.5% and 5.1%, respectively. 'Geography' and 'Math' are the smallest categories, with 'Geography' at 3.7% and 'Math' at 2.2%. Notably, 'Daily Life' has shown a consistent increase in representation compared to previous datasets, while 'Geography' has seen a slight decline.
